_comment: Occupation Trivia Pack. The seller picks an occupation; the pack is about ten numbered multiple-choice questions on that job's tools, terms, routines, traditions and history, each with four lettered choices, and one answer page listing number, letter, answer and a short note. The occupation is a profile (label, who, areas, care, blockedTerms) from the shared occupations data (occupations/prompt.json): one of its hand-written presets, or one the service plans for an occupation the seller typed. Variety is structural: every requested question gets its own brief (one of the occupation's areas and one question shape, sampled by seed). The right answer is its own field, never an index. Nothing ships on the writer's word: a second, blind call sees each question with its choices shuffled, has to pick the right one itself, rates it certain, on-topic, clear, fairly pitched, with believable wrong choices and suitable, flags a question that asks the same fact as an earlier one, and fact-checks every answer-page note on its own. Length budgets arrive on the request; limits below are the hard bounds. qualifierWords are dropped and aliases folded before questions are compared, so 'What tool did teachers use to write on chalkboards?' and 'Which item was used by teachers to write on a blackboard?' read as one question.

locale.nativeLine: - Write in clear, natural English that readers in any English-speaking country can follow.
locale.otherLine: - Write every question, choice and note in language locale '{locale}', about the job as it is known in that language's countries.

gentle.writer: Gentle: knowledge almost anyone who did this job would recognise at once, and that many other adults could work out. Warm and confidence-building.
gentle.checker: someone who worked in this job would very likely know it, and many other adults could work it out

classic.writer: Classic: mostly familiar job knowledge, with a few questions that make a retired professional stop and think for a moment.
classic.checker: someone who spent years in this job would probably know it or enjoy working it out

challenging.writer: Challenging: deeper, lesser-known but well-documented knowledge of the job's tools, terms and history -- the kind a long-serving professional enjoys being tested on. Never specialist exam or certification material.
challenging.checker: a long-serving professional might know it; it is interesting rather than obscure, and never exam or certification material

example.question: Before computers, what did a librarian stamp inside a borrowed book?
example.explanation: A date stamp on the slip in the back of the book showed when it was due.
